name: Air Chopper 7.5SC Insecticide

Air Chopper 7.5SC is a suspension concentrate (SC) insecticide used against all three in Kenyan homes, hostels and small premises. It comes in four pack sizes, from a pack of three 15 ml units up to a 1 litre bottle, and it is diluted in water before spraying.
features: Suspension concentrate (SC) insecticide

Diluted in water before use, as the label directs
Delivered to all 47 counties

Pack sizes: 15 ml (3 pack), 100 ml, 250 ml, 1 litre
Dilution and spray volume: as printed on the label

Cockroaches settle in kitchens, drains and behind cupboards. Ants follow food and trails into rooms and stores. The range of packs lets you match the size to the job, from a smaller pack for a single home to a larger bottle for a hostel block.
use: Read the label first and prepare the dilution exactly as it directs. Spray cracks, crevices, bed frames, skirting boards and the other places where the pests hide or walk. Keep people, pets and food away from treated areas until the label says it is safe to return. Repeat the treatment if the label advises it, and keep the area clean afterwards so that the pests have less to come back for.
before: Clean first: wash bedding and vacuum mattresses, floors and corners
Remove food, and cover utensils and fish tanks before spraying
Treat all the affected rooms in the same visit so the pests do not simply move next door
Call a licensed pest control operator for a large or persistent infestation

faq: What is Air Chopper 7.5SC used for?
It is an insecticide for bed bugs, cockroaches and ants in homes, hostels and small premises.

15 ml in a pack of three, 100 ml, 250 ml and 1 litre. Choose the size that fits the number of rooms or units you need to treat.
How much do I mix?
Follow the dilution and spraying instructions on the label of your pack. The rate is not guessed from the pack size.
Can I get it delivered?
Yes. Pay by M-Pesa for delivery to all 47 counties, or pick up at The Sarit Centre, Westlands, Nairobi.

name: Bat CRP Bat Repellent
lead: Bats that settle in a roof or ceiling leave droppings and urine that stain ceilings, cause strong smells and attract insects, and their noise at night disturbs families, guests and worshippers. Bat CRP is a heavy-duty bat repellent chemical for moving bats out of roofs, ceilings, halls and other hiding places. It is diluted with water as the label directs and comes in 250 ml, 500 ml and 1 litre packs.
features: Heavy-duty bat repellent chemical
For roofs, ceilings, halls and other roosting places
Label dilution for roofing and hall areas: 1 part product to 4 parts water
Three pack sizes: 250 ml, 500 ml and 1 litre
Delivered to all 47 counties
specs: Use: Roofs, ceilings, halls and other roosting places
helps: Droppings build up in roof spaces, and the smell and stains spread to the rooms below. Halls, churches, schools, hotels, offices and homes often need a way to move bats out. Bat CRP is made for that job: you apply the diluted mixture where bats roost, so that they leave and look elsewhere.
dose: Roofing and hall areas: 1 part Bat CRP to 4 parts water
Always confirm the dilution on your pack's label before mixing
use: Dilute Bat CRP with water as directed on the label. Apply the diluted mixture to the places where bats roost, such as the underside of roofs, ceiling spaces, beams and corners. Treat the roosting surfaces thoroughly and repeat if the label advises. Once the bats have left, close the entry points so they cannot return: seal the eaves, gaps around the roof, vents and holes in walls. Then clean up droppings safely and keep the roof space dry and clean.
before: Clear old droppings and wear protective gear first, because dried droppings can create dust
Check local rules on handling bats if you are unsure
safety: Read the label before use. Wear gloves, a mask, goggles and protective clothing when mixing and applying, and use a ladder or platform safely when working at height. Wash your hands after use and keep out of reach of children. Keep away from food, water, pets and livestock, and do not let the product reach streams or ponds.
storage: Store in the original closed container in a cool, dry, locked place.
faq: What is Bat CRP used for?
It is a heavy-duty bat repellent chemical for roofs, ceilings, halls and other places where bats roost in homes and buildings.
How do I dilute it?
Dilute it with water as directed on the label. For roofing and hall areas, the label dilution is 1 part product to 4 parts water.
What should I do after the bats have gone?
Close the entry points, clean up droppings safely and keep the roof space dry.
Will it harm the bats?
It is a repellent. Bats are useful outdoors because they eat insects, so the aim is to move them out of buildings. Check local rules if unsure.

The small 28 ml pack is sized for a house, a bedsitter or a rental unit, so it is easy to buy, store and use for a single treatment. It is an EW formulation, an emulsion in water, that you mix with water for spraying.
features: Insecticide for bed bugs, cockroaches and ants
Small 28 ml pack for homes and rentals
EW formulation: an emulsion in water, mixed with water for spraying
Easy to store between treatments
Delivered to all 47 counties

Dilution and spray volume: as printed on the label
helps: Bed bugs hide in mattress seams, bed frames, headboards and cracks in walls, and they bite at night. Cockroaches shelter in kitchens, drains, cupboards and behind appliances, and they spread germs on food and surfaces. Ants follow food into kitchens, stores and bedrooms and nest in walls, floors and gardens. With one small pack you can treat several of the most common household pests without buying a different product for each.
use: Dilute exactly as directed on the label. Spray cracks, crevices, bed frames, skirting boards, door frames and other hiding places, and spray ant trails and entry points. Keep people, pets and food away until the spray has dried. Repeat the treatment if the label advises it. Treat all the affected rooms at the same time so that the pests do not move to the rooms you have not sprayed.
before: Wash bedding at a high temperature and vacuum mattresses, floors and corners
Remove food and cover utensils before you spray
Check second-hand furniture and luggage for bed bugs before bringing them indoors
For a large or persistent infestation, consider a licensed pest control operator
safety: Read and follow the label before use. Keep away from children, pets, food and water. Wear gloves and a mask when mixing and spraying, and wash your hands afterwards. Do not pour leftover mixture into drains, streams or ponds, and do not reuse the empty bottle.
storage: Keep in the original closed bottle in a cool, dry, locked place.
faq: What pests does Darvin 50EW control?
It is used against bed bugs, cockroaches and ants in homes and rentals.
What does EW mean?
EW stands for emulsion in water. It is a liquid concentrate that you mix with water before spraying.
How can I stop the pests coming back?
Store food in closed containers, wipe up crumbs and spills, keep rubbish bins covered, and seal cracks and gaps around pipes and doors.
Is 28 ml enough for my house?
The pack is sized for a house, a bedsitter or a rental unit. How far it goes depends on the dilution on the label, so check the label before you buy for a larger space.

name: Fendona 60SC Insecticide
lead: Fendona 60SC is a BASF insecticide containing alpha-cypermethrin at 60 g/L, supplied as a water-based suspension concentrate. It is used for public health and household pest control, giving fast knockdown and a lasting residual film on treated surfaces. This 1 litre pack suits homes, hostels, hotels, offices and food premises that need a reliable, professional-grade treatment.
features: Alpha-cypermethrin 60 g/L
Water-based suspension concentrate
Fast knockdown of insects
Lasting residual film on treated surfaces
BASF brand
1 litre pack
Delivered to all 47 counties
specs: Controls: Cockroaches, bed bugs, ants, houseflies, mosquitoes and other insects
helps: A residual insecticide leaves a thin film on the surface after the water dries. Insects that walk across it pick up the active ingredient, so the treatment keeps working for a period after spraying. Because Fendona 60SC is water-based, it can be used on many surfaces in and around buildings.
dose: BASF's published guidance for Fendona 6 SC, routine treatment: 25 ml in 5 litres of water for about 100 m2
Heavy infestations: 50 ml in 5 litres of water
Rates can differ between markets, so always follow the rate printed on your pack
doseTitle: MIXING RATES (BASF GUIDANCE; CONFIRM ON YOUR LABEL)
use: Mix with clean water and apply as a coarse spray to cracks, crevices, skirting edges, behind furniture and other places where insects hide or walk. Shake the bottle well before measuring, because it is a suspension, and mix thoroughly in the sprayer. For hostels, hotels and offices, plan the treatment of the whole building in one go so that insects do not move between rooms.
before: Pay special attention to kitchens, store rooms, drains, door and window frames and bed frames
Keep a simple record of dates, areas treated and rates used
For large buildings or persistent infestations, consider a licensed pest control operator
safety: Do not spray people, pets, food or cooking surfaces. Remove or cover food and utensils, keep children and animals out until surfaces are dry, and wear gloves and a mask. It is very toxic to fish and aquatic life, so never rinse sprayers or empty containers into drains, streams or ponds.
storage: Keep in the original closed bottle in a cool, dry, locked place away from food.
faq: What is the active ingredient in Fendona 60SC?
Alpha-cypermethrin at 60 g/L, in a water-based suspension concentrate. The details are printed on the label.
Which pests does it control?
Cockroaches, bed bugs, ants, houseflies, mosquitoes and other crawling and flying insects in homes, hostels, hotels, offices and food premises.
How much should I mix?
BASF's guidance for Fendona 6 SC is 25 ml in 5 litres of water for about 100 m2, or 50 ml in 5 litres for heavy infestations. Rates differ between markets, so follow your label.
Is it safe near fish ponds and drains?
No. It is very toxic to fish and aquatic life. Never rinse sprayers or empty containers into drains, streams or ponds.

Deltamethrin at 250 g/kg, in a water-dispersible granule (WG). It is made by Envu, formerly Bayer.

Mosquitoes, sand flies, houseflies, fleas, bed bugs and cockroaches in homes, hostels, hotels and public buildings.

name: Promax 20EC Insecticide
lead: Bed bugs (kunguni) hide in mattress seams, bed frames and skirting boards, then bite while you sleep. Promax 20EC is a propoxur-based, odourless insecticide concentrate that you dilute and spray straight into those hiding places. It also tackles cockroaches (mende), fleas, ants and houseflies, so one 1 litre bottle covers a house, hostel, hotel room or office.
features: Odourless formulation suited to bedrooms and other indoor spaces (let surfaces dry fully)
Residual action on treated surfaces, so pests that crawl across later are still affected
Multi-pest: bed bugs, cockroaches, fleas, ants and houseflies
Concentrated: 25 ml makes 1 litre of ready-to-spray liquid
Works with any hand-pump or knapsack sprayer
specs: Use: Household and public-health crawling-insect control
Mode of action: blocks nerve signal transmission, causing paralysis
helps: Most homes need only a small amount of spray, so a concentrate goes a long way: one 1 litre bottle makes 40 litres of ready-to-spray liquid. Bed bugs, cockroaches, fleas, ants and houseflies are the main targets, and the residual film means that pests which crawl across a dry surface later are still affected.
dose: 1 litre hand sprayer: 25 ml Promax 20EC, topped up with water to 1 litre
5 litre garden sprayer: 125 ml, topped up to 5 litres
20 litre knapsack: 500 ml, topped up to 20 litres
Most homes need only 1 to 5 litres; the knapsack rate is for hotels, hostels and large premises
Always confirm the rate on your pack's label before mixing
use: Half-fill the sprayer with clean water, add Promax, top up and shake well. Spray mattress seams, bed frames, headboards, skirting boards, cracks, behind sockets and furniture joints. Wet surfaces lightly; do not soak them. Bed bug eggs can hatch later, so inspect after about two weeks and treat again if needed.
before: Keep children, pets and fish tanks out of the room until surfaces are dry and the room is ventilated
Do not spray food, utensils or bedding you will use before it dries
safety: Wear gloves and wash your hands after use. Read the label before you begin, and keep the bottle out of reach of children.
storage: Keep the bottle closed in a cool, dry, locked place, away from food.
faq: What is Promax 20EC used for?
It is an odourless insecticide concentrate for bed bugs, cockroaches, fleas, ants and houseflies in homes, hostels, hotels and offices.
What is the active ingredient?
Propoxur at 20% w/v, a carbamate insecticide in an emulsifiable concentrate (EC) formulation.
How do I mix it?
25 ml topped up with water to 1 litre in a hand sprayer, 125 ml to 5 litres, or 500 ml to 20 litres. Always confirm the rate on your pack's label.
When should I treat bed bugs again?
Bed bug eggs can hatch later, so inspect after about two weeks and treat again if needed.
